title: Find Valid AI Agent Placements
real_world_story: An AI planning system represents candidate agents as objects that must be placed on a grid without conflicting with one another. Two agents cannot occupy the same row, column, or diagonal.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: N-Queens backtracking to explore candidate placements while avoiding conflicts

problem_statement: Given an integer N, determine the number of ways to place N agents on an N x N grid such that no two agents share the same row, column, or diagonal.
task: Calculate the total number of valid N-agent placements.
input_format: The input contains a single integer N representing the size of the grid.
output_format: Print the total number of valid placements.

examples.explanation: There are exactly two valid ways to place four agents on a 4 x 4 grid without conflicts.
There are ten valid placements for five agents on a 5 x 5 grid.

expected_algorithm.name: N-Queens
expected_algorithm.reason: The N-Queens backtracking approach places one candidate at a time while checking row, column, and diagonal conflicts.

hint: Place one agent in each row.
Before placing an agent, check its column.
Also check both diagonals for conflicts.
Backtrack whenever a placement creates a conflict.
real_world_takeaway: Constraint-based backtracking can be used by AI planning systems to explore candidate arrangements while rejecting invalid configurations early.
